usdRate.note: 1.27808 SGD per USD; the MAS exchange-rate page links only to an interactive tool. World Bank PA.NUS.FCRF gives 1.307 for 2025.

inflation_cpi.sourceName: MAS, Consumer Price Developments in September 2026
inflation_cpi.note: CPI-All Items 2.2% y-o-y in September 2026 (2.3% in August); MAS Core 2.0%. SingStat table M213781 shows the same.

inflation_projection.sourceName: MAS inflation forecasts (CPI-All Items about 2.0% in 2026, 1.5-2.5% in 2027); SingStat CPI 2016-2025 average 1.7%
inflation_projection.note: MAS has no numeric target but treats core inflation just under 2% as consistent with price stability, and forecasts about 2%, so we plan with 2%.

policy_rate.note: MAS runs monetary policy through the exchange rate (S$NEER policy band), not a policy interest rate. The market benchmark SORA averaged 1.40% at end-September 2026 (SingStat M700071).

savings_account_rate.note: MAS stopped publishing average bank savings deposit rates after June 2021 (0.07% then, MAS Interest Rates of Banks and Finance Companies); no official current average was found.

fdr_3m_rate.note: MAS's average 3-month bank fixed deposit series ends in June 2021 (0.12%); no current official average was found.

fdr_1y_rate.note: MAS's average 12-month bank fixed deposit series ends in June 2021 (0.24%); no current official average was found.

dps_rate.note: No standard bank recurring-deposit product or published rate was found for Singapore.

bank_deposit_avg_rate.note: World Bank FR.INR.DPST stops in 2021 (0.12%), when the MAS bank rate series ended; that figure is far below current rates, so it is not used.

sanchayapatra_5y_rate.sourceName: MAS Singapore Savings Bonds, November 2026 issue (GX26110X)
sanchayapatra_5y_rate.note: November 2026 issue (issued 2 November 2026, rates set in October): average return 2.45% a year if held 10 years (1.67% in year 1, stepping up); the 5-year average is not shown by this endpoint. Redeemable any month without penalty; tax-exempt.

tbill_91d_rate.note: 3-month SGS/MAS bill yield 1.87% (Trading Economics, 30 Oct 2026; secondary source, no official 3-month series found on SingStat). Individuals can buy only 6-month and 1-year T-bills; SingStat M700071 shows the 1-year T-bill at 1.73% and 3-month compounded SORA at 1.23% at end-September 2026.

tbond_5y_rate.sourceName: SingStat Table M700071, Government Securities 5-Year Bond Yield (MAS data)
tbond_5y_rate.note: End-September 2026; Trading Economics shows 2.03% on 30 October 2026.

tbond_10y_rate.sourceName: SingStat Table M700071, Government Securities 10-Year Bond Yield (MAS data)
tbond_10y_rate.note: End-September 2026; Trading Economics shows 2.24% on 30 October 2026.

tax_bank_interest.sourceName: PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries, Singapore individual income determination (secondary source)
tax_bank_interest.note: Interest from Singapore-approved banks and licensed finance companies is generally not taxable for individuals; no withholding.

tax_sanchayapatra_profit.sourceName: MAS, Singapore Government T-bills: information for individuals
tax_sanchayapatra_profit.note: For individuals, interest income earned on SGS (including Savings Bonds) is tax exempt.

deposit_insurance_limit.sourceName: Singapore Deposit Insurance Corporation, Deposit Insurance FAQ
deposit_insurance_limit.note: Insured deposits with each scheme member are aggregated and covered up to S$100,000 per depositor.

credit_card_rate_cap.note: No legal cap; the typical effective rate on card balances could not be confirmed from an official page in this pass.

equity_return_low.note: Low case close to the tax-free safe rate.

equity_return_base.note: Tax-free safe rate of about 1.7-1.9% plus a 3.6-point premium; the local index has a modest long-run record, so the premium is kept below 4 points.

equity_return_high.note: High case for a diversified Singapore and global equity mix.

gold_return_low.sourceName: Trading Economics USD/SGD 1.278 (30 Oct 2026), down 1.8% on the year
gold_return_low.note: Low case: flat dollar gold and a firming Singapore dollar.

gold_return_base.sourceName: Trading Economics USD/SGD 1.278 (30 Oct 2026), down 1.8% on the year
gold_return_base.note: Dollar gold trend of about 4% less slow Singapore dollar appreciation under the MAS exchange-rate policy.

gold_return_high.sourceName: Trading Economics USD/SGD 1.278 (30 Oct 2026), down 1.8% on the year
gold_return_high.note: High case with strong dollar gold.

fixed_income_return_low.note: Low case: bank fixed deposits and T-bills if short rates fall, tax-free.

fixed_income_return_base.sourceName: 1-year T-bill 1.73%, 5-year SGS 2.24%, Savings Bond 10-year average 2.45%, all tax-exempt
fixed_income_return_base.note: Base case: a mix of T-bills and Savings Bonds, tax-free.

fixed_income_return_high.sourceName: MAS Singapore Savings Bonds November 2026: 2.45% average over 10 years, tax-exempt
fixed_income_return_high.note: High case: locking in Savings Bonds or 10-year SGS.

life_claim_settlement_rate.note: No industry-wide life claim settlement ratio was found from MAS or the life insurance association.

insurance_term_premium_table.note: Term life is widely sold, but no published per-S$1,000 premium rates by age were retrieved in this pass.

health_hospitalisation_cost.note: MOH publishes bill amounts by procedure through a search tool and fee benchmarks for private single rooms, but no single typical out-of-pocket figure for a major stay was retrieved.

health_premium_table.note: MediShield Life premiums are set per person by age, not per S$100,000 of cover, and Integrated Shield Plan premiums by cover were not retrieved.

oop_health_share.note: Latest World Bank figure is for 2023 (older than 2025).

goal_inflation_health.note: Health CPI ran near 3-4% in recent years with health insurance premiums rising faster, so we plan with 3%.

goal_inflation_education.sourceName: SingStat CPI Education: 0.7% (2025), 3.2% (2024), 2.7% (2023); private tuition 5-6% in 2023-24
goal_inflation_education.note: Education CPI averaged about 2% over ten years with private tuition rising faster, so we plan with 2.5%.

life_expectancy.sourceName: SingStat Table M810501, Life Expectancy at Birth (Residents), preliminary
life_expectancy.note: Residents: men 81.8, women 86.0. World Bank SP.DYN.LE00.IN gives 83.3 for 2024 (total population).

life_table_remaining.sourceName: UN World Population Prospects 2024 via populationpyramid.net
life_table_remaining.note: Secondary source of UN WPP 2024 medium variant for 2026; totals at 60, 70 and 80 are the mean of men and women. SingStat gives 21.6 years at 65 for residents in 2025 (men 19.9, women 23.1).

support_ratio.sourceName: World Bank SP.POP.DPND.OL (2025); UN WPP 2024 via populationpyramid.net (2040, 2065)
support_ratio.note: 100 / old-age dependency ratio: 19.18 (2025, World Bank), 32.0 (2040) and 78.4 (2065, populationpyramid.net/singapore/2065/).

retirement_age_default.sourceName: CPF Board, CPF LIFE (payouts from age 65)
retirement_age_default.note: CPF LIFE payouts start from 65 (deferrable to 70), which applies to members born after 1975. The statutory minimum retirement age under the Retirement and Re-employment Act is 64 from 1 July 2026 (MOM), with re-employment beyond it.

retirement_age_government.note: No separate civil-service retirement age was confirmed from an official page; the statutory minimum retirement age for employees is 64 from 1 July 2026 (MOM, https://www.mom.gov.sg/employment-practices/retirement), which public officers are believed to follow.

retirement_return_low.note: Low case if short-term rates fall back, tax-free.

retirement_return_base.note: Base case at the tax-free 1-year T-bill rate.

retirement_return_high.sourceName: MAS Singapore Savings Bonds November 2026: 2.45% average over 10 years, tax-exempt
retirement_return_high.note: High case: laddered Savings Bonds and SGS.

retirement_accumulation_return_low.note: Low case for a balanced mix if equities only match bonds.

retirement_accumulation_return_base.sourceName: Equity base 5.5% and SGS/Savings Bonds about 2-2.5%; CPF LIFE savings earn at least 4%
retirement_accumulation_return_base.note: Base case: roughly half equity and half safe bonds.

retirement_accumulation_return_high.note: High case with the equity high case.

old_age_allowance_monthly.note: Silver Support Scheme, means-tested quarterly payouts (raised in 2025): up to S$1,080 a quarter (S$360 a month) for 1- and 2-room HDB flat dwellers with per capita household income up to S$1,500, down to S$215 a quarter for 5-room flats with income S$1,500-2,300. Paid automatically to eligible citizens from 65.

old_age_allowance_eligibility.note: Singapore Citizens 65 and above; lifetime CPF contributions by 55 up to S$140,000, 1- to 5-room HDB flat, per capita household income up to S$2,300 a month. No application needed.

gratuity_rule.note: No statutory gratuity or end-of-service benefit: MOM's Responsible retrenchment guidance says the retrenchment benefit depends on the employment contract or collective agreement, or must be negotiated (norm 2 weeks to 1 month's salary per year of service for 2+ years' service); no law sets one.

public_pension_scheme.sourceName: CPF Board, CPF LIFE; PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries (CPF benefits excluded from taxable retirement benefits)
public_pension_scheme.note: CPF is a mandatory contributory scheme for citizen and PR employees; CPF LIFE pays a monthly annuity for life from 65 (Standard plan level; Escalating plan rises 2% a year; neither is indexed to inflation). PwC: 'All retirement benefits other than CPF benefits ... are generally taxable' (https://taxsummaries.pwc.com/singapore/individual/income-determination). Official payout examples were not retrieved.

savings_account.note: Bank savings deposits; MAS stopped publishing average rates in 2021.

dps.note: No standard bank recurring-deposit product was identified; monthly savings plans are usually investment plans.

sanchayapatra_5y.note: 10-year government bond for individuals with step-up interest; buy from S$500 monthly, redeem any month without penalty; tax-exempt.

tbill_91d.note: Individuals can buy 6-month and 1-year T-bills at auction from S$1,000; 3-month bills are not offered to individuals.

tbond_5y.note: Individuals can bid at SGS bond auctions.

equity_fund.note: Diversified unit trusts and exchange-traded index funds are widely available to retail investors.

gold.note: Gold bars and coins can be bought freely.

insuranceRegulator.name: Monetary Authority of Singapore
insuranceRegulator.note: MAS is the integrated regulator for banks and insurers.

publicHealthCover.name: Ministry of Health (MediShield Life)
publicHealthCover.note: MediShield Life, the universal basic health insurance run with the CPF Board.
